content.title: Guideline excerpts - Heart Failure recommendations (2021 vs 2016)

items.recommendation: Invasive coronary angiography may be considered in patients with HFrEF with an intermediate to high pre-test probability of CAD and the presence of ischaemia in non-invasive stress tests.

CT coronary angiography (CTCA) should be considered in patients with a low to intermediate pre-test probability of CAD or those with equivocal non-invasive stress tests to rule out coronary artery stenosis.
Cardiac CT may be considered in patients with HF and low to intermediate pre-test probability of CAD or those with equivocal non-invasive stress tests in order to rule out coronary artery stenosis.

sections.section_title: Recommendations for device therapy in HFrEF

items.recommendation: An ICD should be considered to reduce the risk of sudden death and all-cause mortality in patients with symptomatic HFrEF (NYHA class II–III) of non-ischaemic aetiology, and an LVEF ≤35% despite ≥3 months of OMT, provided they are expected to survive substantially longer than 1 year with good functional status.
Primary prevention ICD in selected patients (similar wording) was Class I in 2016 but IIa in 2021 (update reflects nuanced indications).

CRT should be considered for symptomatic patients with HF in sinus rhythm with QRS duration 130–149 ms and LBBB QRS morphology and with LVEF ≤35% despite OMT to improve symptoms and reduce morbidity and mortality.
Patients with LVEF ≤35% who have a conventional pacemaker or an ICD and subsequently develop worsening HF despite OMT and with a high proportion of RV pacing should be considered for upgrade to CRT.

sections.section_title: Recommendations for management of patients with acute HF

items.recommendation: Combination of a loop diuretic with a thiazide-type diuretic should be considered in patients with resistant oedema who do not respond to an increase in loop diuretic doses.
In patients with AHF and SBP >110 mmHg, IV vasodilators may be considered as initial therapy to improve symptoms and reduce congestion.
Routine use of opioids is not recommended; opioids may be considered for cautious use to relieve dyspnoea and anxiety in selected patients with severe dyspnoea.

Short-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS) should be considered in patients with cardiogenic shock as a bridge to recovery, decision, or long-term therapy depending on cause, comorbidities and neurological function.

sections.section_title: Recommendations for management of patients with HF and AF

items.recommendation: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are recommended in preference to VKAs in patients with HF and non-valvular AF, except in those with moderate or severe mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic heart valves.

For patients with HF and non-valvular AF eligible for anticoagulation, a CHA2DS2-VASc based approach recommends NOACs rather than warfarin; NOACs associated with lower risk of stroke, intracranial haemorrhage and mortality.
Beta-blockers should be considered for short- and long-term rate control in patients with HF and AF.

AV node catheter ablation may be considered to control heart rate and relieve symptoms in patients unresponsive or intolerant to pharmacological rate and rhythm control, accepting patients may become pacemaker-dependent.

sections.section_title: Recommendations for management of patients with HF and CCS (chronic coronary syndrome)

items.recommendation: Coronary revascularization should be considered to relieve persistent symptoms of angina in patients with HF and CCS, and myocardial revascularization is recommended when angina persists despite treatment with anti-anginal drugs.

sections.section_title: Recommendations for management of patients with HF and diabetes

items.recommendation: SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM at risk of cardiovascular events to reduce hospitalizations for HF, major CV events, end-stage renal dysfunction, and CV death.
Empagliflozin should be considered in patients with T2DM in order to prevent or delay the onset of HF and prolong life.
